### A. The amalgamation (`8832cfd20`)

- **v4 at the pin.** `package.json:78` `"better-sqlite3":
  "npm:better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers@^13.0.3"`; `package-lock.json:6881-
  6885` `node_modules/better-sqlite3` → `better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers`
  `13.0.3`, integrity `sha512-UYabM82r1J84TLWc/SszoHs6XopWpl/2HCg3Nui1JUaF
  Xg/VLswzkPowYiRhK/4CftI8dgtikwyZQecMldrGxQ==`. `packages/quilltap/
  package.json:40` `"better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers": "^13.0.3"`. (At
  `236c04e35`: `12.11.1`, lock `:7437-7440`.)
- **What the driver bundles [measured, from the 13.0.3 install, which the
  pin's lockfile reproduces]:** `deps/sqlite3/sqlite3.c` (13,019,798
  bytes, sha256 `ad84d2c2…0614a0`), `deps/sqlite3/sqlite3.h` (699,088
  bytes, sha256 `eae796d6…967374`), `deps/sqlite3/sqlite3ext.h`,
  `deps/defines.gypi`. `sqlite3.h:36` `#define SQLITE3MC_VERSION_STRING
  "SQLite3 Multiple Ciphers 2.4.0"`, `:195` `#define SQLITE_VERSION
  "3.53.4"`, `:197` `SQLITE_SOURCE_ID "2026-07-24 19:02:57
  bf7c7f30031888f4e796e429ab3978879485813aaca6f641c7b33e4e09459bcc"`. Both
  files are LF-terminated in 13.0.3. Re-measure every number above in YOUR
  pin's install before vendoring and record them; the pin's bytes win.
- **How the driver BUILDS that amalgamation** (`deps/update-sqlite3mc.sh`,
  `YEAR=2026 VERSION=3530400 SQLITE3MC_VERSION=v2.4.0`): it builds SQLite's
  OWN amalgamation from the canonical source with `make OPTIONS="$CFLAGS"
  sqlite3.c` (the CFLAGS = every define in `defines.gypi`), patches it with
  SQLite3MC's `patchsqlite3.sh` / `rekeyvacuum.sh`, and re-amalgamates with
  SQLite3MC's `amalgamate.py`. **Consequence: the driver's `sqlite3.c` is
  GENERATED WITH v4's defines** — its parser is built from `parse.y` "with
  these options: -DSQLITE_ENABLE_UPDATE_DELETE_LIMIT" and it defines
  `SQLITE_UDL_CAPABLE_PARSER 1` near its top. SQLite documents that
  `SQLITE_OMIT_*` and grammar-affecting options belong to amalgamation
  GENERATION; compiling a generated amalgamation with a different option set
  is unsupported territory. That is why this order's "source the driver's
  exact bytes" and "defines parity" are ONE decision, not two.
- **⚠ Survey correction — provenance of today's vendor.** The survey says
  "drop the 2.4.0 amalgamation `.c` / `.h` into `vendor/` … No flag change".
  **[measured]** v5's CURRENT vendor (`sqlite3mc_amalgamation.c`,
  12,986,405 bytes, sha256 `ff621c6b…86b45e5`; `.h` sha256 `bb0087cf…
  8d8493`) is **NOT** what v4's 12.11.1 driver bundled: the 12.11.1
  tarball (`npm pack better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers@12.11.1 --offline
  --cache ~/.npm-clean` — cached) ships CRLF files whose LF-normalised `.h`
  is IDENTICAL to v5's, but whose LF-normalised `.c` differs in 858 diff
  lines — exactly the UDL parser (`#define SQLITE_UDL_CAPABLE_PARSER 1` at
  `:154`, `YYNSTATE 604` vs `600`, the parse.y options comment at
  `:179854`). v5 vendored **utelle's release amalgamation** (generated with
  no options), not the driver's. The 12.11.1 and 13.0.3 `defines.gypi` are
  byte-identical. So "matching what v4 bundles" has never been literally
  true of the `.c`; this lane makes it true.
- **v4's `defines.gypi` at the pin [measured, 38 entries]:** `HAVE_INT16_T=1
  HAVE_INT32_T=1 HAVE_INT8_T=1 HAVE_STDINT_H=1 HAVE_UINT16_T=1

### B. `quilltap db integrity` (`70d2859d8`)

- **v4 at the pin** (`packages/quilltap/lib/db-commands.js`):
  - `:1349-1353` `OPTIMIZE_TARGETS` = `{ 'main': {filename: 'quilltap.db',
    label: 'main'}, 'llm-logs': {filename: 'quilltap-llm-logs.db', label:
    'llm-logs'}, 'mount-points': {filename: 'quilltap-mount-index.db',
    label: 'mount-points'} }`; `:1504` `INTEGRITY_TARGETS =
    OPTIMIZE_TARGETS`.
  - `:1661-1728` `cmdIntegrity`: `parseSubArgs`; `--json` via `asBool`;
    no positional or `['all']` → every target, else each positional looked
    up — a miss throws `Unknown integrity target '<p>'. Allowed: main |
    llm-logs | mount-points | all`. `getLockStatus(ctx.dataDir)` and, when
    NOT json and the state is `active` or `suspect`: `Live instance
    detected<pidPart> — running read-only checks.` (`pidPart` = ` (PID
    <n>)` when the lock carries a pid). Per target: a missing file →
    (not json) `Skipping <label>: <dbPath> not found.` and `{target, ok:
    false, openable: false, issues: [], reason: 'not found'}`. Then
    `anyOpenFailed = some(openable === false && reason !== 'not found')`,
    `anyIssues = some(openable !== false && !ok)`. JSON → `printJson({
    results })`; else a blank line and ONE of `All databases reported ok.`
    / `One or more databases could not be opened.` / `One or more
    databases reported integrity issues — see above.` (open failure WINS
    over issues). Then `anyOpenFailed` → throw `database open failure`
    with `silent = true`, `exitCode = 2`; else `anyIssues` → throw
    `integrity issues detected`, `silent`, `exitCode = 1`.
  - `:1730-1787` `integrityOneDb`: prints a blank line and `── <label>
    (<dbPath>) ──` (two spaces before the parenthesis) **UNCONDITIONALLY —
    also under `--json`** (a v4 quirk: the JSON follows the human blocks;
    the same shape v5's `optimize_one_db` already reproduces). Opens with
    `openMainDb` / `openLlmLogsDb` / `openMountIndexDb` `{readonly: true}`;
    an open throw → `  open failed: <err.message>` and `{target, ok:
    false, openable: false, issues: [], reason: err.message}`. Then
    `db.pragma('integrity_check')`; a THROW → `lines = ['page read failed
    (<err.code || 'error'>): <err.message>']`; else the rows' first column,
    falsy dropped. `lines` exactly `['ok']` → `integrityCheck = 'ok'` and
    `  integrity_check: ok` (ONE space — it was eight before the commit);
    else `integrityCheck = lines.join('; ')` and per line `
    integrity_check: <line>` + `issues.push({pragma: 'integrity_check',
    message: line})`. Close; `  duration: <formatDuration(ms)>`. Answer
    `{target, ok: integrityCheck === 'ok', openable: true, integrityCheck,
    issues, durationMs}` — `cipherIntegrityCheck` / `cipherCheck` GONE.
    The why-comment (`:1744-1749`: SQLite3MC has no `cipher_integrity_
    check`; every page `integrity_check` reads must decrypt and pass its
    Poly1305 tag, and a failing page throws SQLITE_CORRUPT / SQLITE_NOTADB)
    is carried forward verbatim in substance.
  - `lib/db-helpers.js:176-226` `openEncryptedDb` (missing → `<friendly>
    not found: <path>`; `pragma key = "x'<hex>'"`; `SELECT 1` probe → throw

  - `bin/quilltap.js:912-920`: `runVerb` catch prints `Error: <message>`

  - Help bytes `bin/quilltap.js:806-811` and `:855` (the diff of the span

## Tiered deliverables

### Tier 1 — must land (three commits, in this order)

**Commit A — `deps(sqlite3mc): vendor SQLite3MC 2.4.0 / SQLite 3.53.4 from
v4's driver 13.0.3, defines at parity` (items 1–3; sys 0.2.0, core +1).**

1. **Re-vendor the amalgamation, byte-exact from the pin's driver, and
   bring the defines to parity.**
   - **Red first (§R.7), on unported `main`, BEFORE touching the sys
     crate:** write the NEW build-parity differential (item 2) and run it
     against the pin's driver. Expected red (record each): `sqlite_version`
     `3.53.2` ≠ `3.53.4`; `sqlite3mc_version` `… 2.3.5` ≠ `… 2.4.0`; the
     `compile_options` diff (v4-only rows such as `DEFAULT_FOREIGN_KEYS`,
     `DQS=0`, `ENABLE_STAT4`, `ENABLE_FTS3`, `ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS`,
     `LIKE_DOESNT_MATCH_BLOBS`, `OMIT_DEPRECATED`, `THREADSAFE=2` vs v5's
     value…, and any v5-only rows) — the full two-way list, by name, in the
     lane record. `PRAGMA cipher` = `chacha20` is EXPECTED GREEN already
     (both sides default to sqleet) and must stay green.
   - **Vendor:** copy `"$PIN/node_modules/better-sqlite3/deps/sqlite3/
     sqlite3.c"` → `crates/quilltap-sqlite3mc-sys/vendor/
     sqlite3mc_amalgamation.c`, `…/sqlite3.h` →
     `vendor/sqlite3mc_amalgamation.h`, and `…/deps/defines.gypi` →
     `vendor/defines.gypi` — `cp`, then `cmp` each against its source and
     record the three sha256s and byte counts. **No line-ending or any other
     normalisation** (13.0.3's are LF; if YOUR pin's are CRLF, STOP and
     report — that would mean the pin's install is not the planner-measured
     one). Keep the vendored file names (`sqlite3mc_amalgamation.{c,h}`) so
     `locate_amalgamation` and `SQLITE3MC_AMALGAMATION_DIR` keep working;
     the docblock records that the bytes are the driver's `sqlite3.{c,h}`.
     `sqlite3ext.h` is NOT needed (v5 loads no extensions) — record that
     you left it out.
   - **Defines — parity is the default; a hold is named and measured.**
     `build.rs` READS `vendor/defines.gypi` (a tiny line parser: every
     `'NAME'` / `'NAME=VALUE'` entry between `'defines': [` and `]`, in
     file order) and passes each to `cc::Build::define` — so the ONE source
     of truth is v4's own file, and a future re-vendor moves both together.
     A `HELD: &[(&str, &str)]` table in `build.rs` (define name → the named
     reason, e.g. `("SQLITE_DEFAULT_FOREIGN_KEYS", "SQLITE_DEFAULT_FK_HELD")`)
     is subtracted from that list, each entry printed as a
     `cargo:warning=` — EMPTY unless the decision rule below fills it. v5's
     two v4-absent defines `SQLITE_HAS_CODEC` and
     `SQLITE3MC_USE_RANDOM_FILL_MEMORY` are DROPPED for parity (v4 runs
     without them; the cipher proof in item 2 is the measurement that
     dropping them is safe — if `PRAGMA cipher` or a cross-open goes red,
     STOP and report rather than restore them unexplained).
     `SQLITE_USE_URI` becomes `=0` per v4 (v5's opens pass
     `SQLITE_OPEN_URI` where needed — the grep in §A's URI bullet is the
     measurement).
   - **The decision rule (the planner's; the lane applies it, it does not
     re-litigate it):** build with FULL parity first. Then run, in order:
     the item-2 differential; the item-3 fixture guard; `cargo test -p
     quilltap-core --lib`; the workspace gate (one run, §R.9). A red is
     attributed to a define ONLY by flipping that one define into `HELD`
     and re-running the red binary by name (each flip is a cold
     amalgamation recompile — expect ~4 minutes per flip, so attribute by
     reasoning first: an FK error text → `DEFAULT_FOREIGN_KEYS`; a LIKE over
     a BLOB → `LIKE_DOESNT_MATCH_BLOBS`; a link error → the `OMIT_*` that
     removed the symbol; a URI open → `USE_URI`). A define stays HELD
     only when (a) it alone explains a red, AND (b) that red is in a family
     this lane does not own or is a v5 test fixture's premise (an FK-off
     helper), never a production-behaviour divergence from v4. A red that
     shows v5 PRODUCTION code disagreeing with v4 under v4's define is a
     FINDING — record it by name, keep the define converged if the fix is
     in your files, otherwise HOLD it and HANDOFF the finding (H3). The
     expected outcomes: `ENABLE_STAT4` CONVERGES (its two tripwires retire,
     item 1's last bullet); `DQS=0` CONVERGES (the P4.172 runtime call
     already made v5 behave so); `DEFAULT_FOREIGN_KEYS` is the likeliest
     HOLD (`SQLITE_DEFAULT_FK_HELD` — production parity is already
     achieved by the writer's explicit `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`).
   - **The STAT4 tripwires retire by measurement (both legs):**
     `daily_db_optimize_equivalence`'s `STAT4_NOT_COMPILED` table and its
     `build_has_stat4` branch become a POSITIVE assertion that v4's and
     v5's `sqlite_stat4` row counts and post-`ANALYZE` sizes now AGREE (or
     the size/page-count parity the table was masking — run it from the
     pin and record what it measures); `cli_differential`'s

     `build_has_stat4()` guard already compares raw sizes once the build
     has STAT4 — confirm the `db optimize` rows go green RAW, then delete
     the dead normaliser and the pin, or keep the pin inverted as "the
     build HAS STAT4"). If STAT4 had to be HELD, both tripwires stay

## The differential requirement, restated

Every ported unit ships an equivalence test driving v4's REAL code at the
pin: item 1–2 is **tier 1 exact** against v4's REAL driver binary (the pin's
`better-sqlite3-multiple-ciphers` 13.0.3, loaded by Node — never a constant
copied from this order); item 3 is a guard over committed bytes; item 4 is
**Tier R** — byte-diffed stdout + stderr + exit code against v4's REAL CLI
at the pin (`$PIN/packages/quilltap/bin/quilltap.js`, its floor-installed
driver), plus a source-text guard over the pin's `constants.cpp`; item 5 is
**tier 1 exact** against v4's REAL croner 11.0.0 resolved from the pin's
`node_modules`. Families this lane regenerates (§R.13: "Croner and the CLI
Tier R `db integrity` → P4.D365"), each ONCE from the pin:
`enclave_cron_equivalence` (both zones), `sqlite_build_parity_equivalence`
(NEW), `cli_differential` (whole, once — the new rows + `db --help` + the
`db optimize` STAT4 rows), `daily_db_optimize_equivalence` (the STAT4
retirement). Re-run from the pin, expected UNMOVED (record each):
`enclave_lifecycle_tier2_equivalence`, `chat_create_capstone_equivalence`,
`degraded_sibling_open_equivalence`, `host_boot_hardness`, every DB family
the workspace gate covers (they now run on 2.4.0 — any red is a finding
attributed per item 1's rule).

Closest recipes / cases to copy: `harness/oracle/cases/enclave-cron.ts` +
`crates/quilltap-harness/tests/enclave_cron_equivalence.rs` (item 5, and
the probe-row idiom for item 2); `crates/quilltap-harness/tests/
daily_db_optimize_equivalence.rs:511-556` (the `PRAGMA compile_options`
read and a named both-ways table); `crates/quilltap-cli/tests/
cli_differential.rs:3404-3447` (the `db optimize` block — durations,
`--json`, named targets, the bogus target) and its `rekeyed()` / lock /
`db unreadable database` pre-hooks; `crates/quilltap-cli/src/db_cmd.rs`
`cmd_optimize` / `optimize_one_db` (the twin). Memory notes that apply:
`oracle-runner-and-skip-traps` (SKIP reports `ok`; confirm by name with
`--nocapture`), `tier-r-vacuous-equal-rows` (self-checking plants),
`sqlite-stat4-build-difference` and `sqlite-dqs-build-difference` (what
retires), `sweep-driver-spaced-path`, `sweep-driver-recipe-header-rules`,

- **§R.8 — The unifier's accumulation.**
  - Each lane's record states its `Cargo.toml` versions at close. The
    unifier takes the HIGHEST and bumps +1 for the union commit;
    `Cargo.lock` follows. The SPA takes the highest of the SPA lanes, +1.
  - CHANGELOG entries and `status-log.md` lane records union-merge
    (append-only).
  - **Shared-index rule:** commit with `git commit -- <paths>`, never
    `git add -A` (memory note `unify-review-finding-shapes`).
- **§R.9 — One machine.**
  - **Workspace gates:** at most TWO Rust workspace gates at once.
    - Count them with ONE `ps -ax -o pid,etime,command | grep "cargo test
      --workspace" | grep -v grep`.
    - If two are running, queue yours in ONE background command that waits
      on the siblings' PIDs, then re-counts once after the wait. Never wait
      on a pattern (memory notes `no-pattern-kill-on-shared-machine`,
      `parallel-lane-shared-resources`).
  - **Sweeps and Playwright:** one sweep at a time (announced). One
    Playwright run at a time: lanes run by file only; the full suite is the
    unifier's.
    - New own-instance e2e server ports are unique per lane (P4.D368 edits
      the existing `salon-storyteller-flow.spec.ts` on its 4353 / 45351 and
      takes none): **P4.D384 4361 / 45359**, **P4.D385 4362 /
      45360**, **P4.D386 4363 / 45361**, **P4.D387 4364 / 45362**,
      **P4.D388 4365 / 45363**, **P4.D383 4366 / 45364** (a11y only).
    - A lane that only edits an EXISTING spec takes no port.
  - **Long jobs:** `run_in_background: true`, with the full log in a
    lane-private file, awaited by the completion notification.
    - NEVER a `pgrep`/`grep` poll loop (CLAUDE.md). Never `tail -N` on a
      gate log.
    - No regen and no source edit while a gate runs (memory note
      `lane-gate-hygiene`).
  - **Targets:**
    - Clone main's `target/` before the first build (`cp -cR`; same volume
      only). Main's `target/` was warmed by this round's `/setupphase`
      chain at the orders' commit.
    - A stacked lane may instead clone its parent's worktree target when
      the parent is not mid-build.
    - **P4.D365's sys bump recompiles the amalgamation in ITS lane only.**
  - **`apps/web/dist/`:** build it before any workspace clippy / test.
    **`apps/web/node_modules`:** run `npm ci` in the lane (a cloned copy
    fails every vitest spec with NG0203).
  - **Concurrency:** the cap is the two-gate rule, not the lane count. The
    waves are in §S.0.
